utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Today is Tuesday, the 8th of July, 2008. Good morning to the accused, to the Defence counsel, to Mr. Stringer and his assistants, as well as to all people assisting us in this case. We are going to proceed with the examination-in-chief, and let me greet Mr. Karnavas again whilst giving him the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Buntic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, we will need your assistance to give Mr. Buntic his binder. We had to re-arrange some documents and, Your Honours, you will see there is a list we provided for you which sort of traces the -- our intent, how we will proceed, how the documents are arranged. So this may provide you some assistance in following along as we go from document to document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe you were more or less finished with your answer to eh question concerning document P 00292; so, therefore, I will move on to the next document which is P 09552; P 09552, it's a P document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The list, Your Honours, that list that we provided, I believe -- in any event. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at this particular document, and it says "Order" in English. Is this an order, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decree; this is not an order. I spoke yesterday about this document here. This is a decree on the organization, operation, and jurisdiction of judiciary in case of a state of war or imminent war threat in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; and, also, I said yesterday that this decree was discussed and adopted at the Presidency session on the 3rd of July, 1992, but that it never --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, you will need to slow down. The translators will not be able to keep up with you. So please slow down, and just let me lead you very quickly through this document. Was this -- you said it was adopted. Was it ever published, this particular decree?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree was never published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, nor was it ever applied. It was passed and adopted, but it was immediately after that, on the 17th of October, that a new decree was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, we have some 100 documents to go through, and we will not be able to go through the document, unless you allow me to sort of lead you. We will get to that document in due course. That's all I needed for this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions, we will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We will discuss this document when we get to the one that was actually passed, published, and applied concerning the judiciary. Okay. If we go on to the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions on this document, I will go to next document which is P 00305, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can see that this is a decision to establish the Official Gazette. My first question is: Why was it necessary to establish an Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Official Gazette was established for the transparency of the work of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. In this particular case, this is about the documents of the Presidency. As is known everywhere, every municipality in the former Yugoslavia had its Official Gazette; thus, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna deemed it necessary to have its own official publication to publish all the regulations that were adopted by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, it's interesting that you say that because we had a witness here by the name of Ciril Ribicic who was on the constitutional court of Slovenia; and what he said on 10 December 2007, page 25498, line 10 to 19, I will be reading. "Q. And what role did the Narodni List play in the governmental structure or legal structure of Herceg-Bosna?" Answer from our constitutional expert from Slovenia; Prosecution witness, that is. He says: "Narodni List published all decisions passed by the bodies of the community of Herceg-Bosna. That was the Official Gazette such as the states have in order to publish their laws and other regulations. One should also mention that in the former state within the republics of the former Yugoslavia, even the municipalities published their own regulations in the Official Gazettes, but," and I underscore this word, "but not a gazette that was their own; rather, in the Official Gazette of the republic that they belonged to." So my question now is: Is Ribicic correct when he says that in the former system, the municipalities did not have the right or did not have Narodni List Official Gazette, and they could only publish their regulations in the Official Gazette of the republic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect to Professor Ribicic, I believe that his words are absolutely wrong, because the documents that you showed me yesterday show a number of instances where the municipalities published their regulations in the Official Gazettes of the municipalities. Not only I but every professional in law should be aware of the fact that every municipality in the former Yugoslavia had its own Official Gazette in which they published regulations adopted by the respective municipalities, and it was not just one municipality that had that. Every single municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the period leading up to the war and during the war had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, if we go on to the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions, I will move on to the next document, and that is 1D 01558, 1D 01558. It's dated September 12th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see that it's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, and I just want to -- I'm going to move through some of these documents rather quickly, Mr. Buntic, based on your previous answers yesterday, the narrative. You talked about legal vacuums that were created; and, here, we see, for instance, Mr. Prlic saying in the very first paragraph that -- that he's enclosing some acts that were passed by the temporary executive and administrative body. Then later on, on the second paragraph, he indicates that with the decree of the president of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated May 2, 1992, certain regulations have been inherited from the former SFRY, while other regulations are declared null and void. By declaring those regulations null and void, a legal vacuum has been created, the consequences of which is a fact that the whole fields, especially in economy, remain unregulated. So this is what you meant yesterday when you talked about the passage of a law at the Presidency level, at the state level, and the legal vacuums that were created; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I'm aware of this letter sent by the president of the HVO, Jadranko Prlic, and sent to the Government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And this confirms what we just said about the transparency of the HVO's work, and it is also in keeping with what I was saying yesterday about the legal vacuums that occurred after the breakup of the former Yugoslavia and after the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted documents, pronouncing null and void some of the regulations that had been implemented in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina up to then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to cover two documents. I put them in the housekeeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me go back to one document, 1D 02441. I skipped this document; it was an error on my part. This is just a press release.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's dated 3 July 1992, and this more or less finishes our topic because we have been dealing with legislation that were passed as a result of that -- those meetings held on that day. And, here, it indicates on paragraph -- on first paragraph, there's a last sentence. It says: "These decisions in no way impinge on the sovereignty and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. All these decisions are in accordance with EC principles on the constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina as an independent state." So my question to you, Mr. Buntic, is: Do you agree with this part of the press release that was sent out by Mate Boban; that is, that the legislation that was being enacted did not infringe or impinge on the sovereignty and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely agree with this, with this release. And I know that it was published immediately after the Presidency session on the 3rd of July, 1992, and that it was published in some dailies immediately after the closing of the session. It also speaks of the transparency of the work of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna about its true goals and intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And now going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, this document is signed by Boban. Can you tell us, do you know who drafted it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure, and I'd rather not speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could it be yourself. The formulations, could they come from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there were discussions about this, but I wouldn't say that I was the author of this document. We discussed this after the session of the Presidency, but there were other documents to this same effect, not only this one. I believe that there were several press releases after this session, after we had discussed this subject; and, yes, I did discuss the subject with Boban, but I'm not sure that I actually drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just two matters I wanted to get out of the way because they don't fit into any particular topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to 1D 02117, and -- it's 1D 02117, 1D 02117.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is a conclusion, and it deals with the amounts of advanced payments on salaries. And, yesterday, you indicated how the president -- the HVO, executive authority, worked and that everyone had one vote, and the purpose of this is to show the salaries. And we can see that the president, vice-president, and heads of department, they all received the same salaries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this conclusion is correct and that this is what was paid in reality, and that the ratios that existed at the time were as shown in this conclusion. I don't know whether it should be noted that these amounts translate into a minute amounts of money, maybe 150 euro for president and vice-presidents; whereas, the others received even less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the whole purpose was to show that everybody's getting paid the same amount; that's the primary focus of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we move on to the next document, 1D 00126, again it's sort of what I would call a housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decision on the appointment of the commission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You say it shows -- the document shows that everyone gets the same amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But it has a whole list of six different --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- steps going from 50.000 down to 20.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps -- perhaps I didn't articulate myself correctly or maybe it was lost in translation. I was saying the department heads - the president, the vice-president - the department heads get paid the same. The point being is Dr. Jadranko Prlic is first among equals, and that when he signs a document, it's not his decision. It's a decision of the executive authority, and obviously -- and also we can see from this document that there are other heads and subdepartment heads which also might assist you, Judge Trechsel, when you pose that question as to who the others might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just a very quick objection to the argument or statement of counsel characterizing the document. I think the witness is here to talk about it and not counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree with the Prosecutor. I was merely invited to respond to Your Honour's question, which I thought you were -- since I wasn't clear enough the first time, I tried to be as clear and forth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I probably made also mistake because I ought to have, in a technique similar to cross-examination, put the question directly to the witness. It was my courtesy that I address myself to you, and please do not take grudge from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. But I take the Prosecution's point and I'll try to remedy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00126. This is just a decision, and we see that it's for the appointment of the commission of regulations of the Croatian Defence Council. It's dated 27 November 1992. First, if you can tell us: What is this commission for regulations, if you know very quickly, in one sentence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a commission that proposed various regulations, very often even drafted them, and then evaluated the congruency of these regulations with regulations of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the other regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And this would be the shortest I can tell you about the commission for regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at the names, can we draw any conclusions as to the ethnicity of those who were being appointed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two Bosniaks, Muslims, in the commission, and two Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an equal representation, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to go through another set of documents, and this deals with other statutory decisions from other municipalities. And, Mr. Buntic, I would be ever so kind -- I would appreciate it very, very much if you could be very short, because we don't need to go through these documents unless the Trial Chamber has questions, and then feel free to expand as much as you think is necessary. But we just need to show these documents to the Trial Chamber to get an idea of what the other municipalities were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 02261, 1D 02261. This is a statutory decision of Bosanska Posavina, and we see this is 11 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You would have been familiar with this statutory decision at some point or another; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the Croatian Community of Bosanska Posavina adopted this statutory decision, which, in my view, provides a much simpler and clearer solutions to the internal organization, and the functioning that may be the statutory decision of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I'm familiar with this decision, and this decision also points to the fact that different communities had different regulations, which also points to the fact that they were not synchronised in their activities, that they're activities were not planned in advance. Everybody made do as they could within the given situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in keeping with that answer, let's look at the next document and we'll -- and other documents as well, and we'll be able to see that at a glance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 01925, 1925. This is a -- this deals with the region of North-Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we see that it talks about the Croatian Defence Council as a political organization with the following objectives and tasks. If we look at the very last page, we see that this was signed on 12 June 1992 in Tuzla; and, of course, you must have been aware of the -- of this document as well and the municipalities that it covered?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document providing to the establishment of the founding of the municipalities of Tuzla, Zivnice, Kalesija, Lukavac, Gracanica, Srebrenik, Gradacac, Lopare, Brcko. I know that the HVO was established in these areas as well, and that later on these communities or parts thereof served for the establishment of the Croatian community of Soli.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we'll come to that with the next few documents. We just need to move rather quickly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just a very small question. Are all these communities we've now been looking at documents, are they part of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The community Soli -- actually, subsequently, some of these communities joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I'm referring to the Croatian Community of Bosanska Posavina. And some decisions were also issued providing for the joining of other municipalities once the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was established on the 18th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. But at the time of these documents, they were not or some were not members or did not belong to Herceg-Bosna, or did they already belong to Herceg-Bosna at the time of the documents we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be said that, first, the Croatian community of Bosanska Posavina was established around the 11th of December, 1992, and that only subsequently it joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It should also be said that in some of the parts of these communities that we just mentioned or these municipalities. Later on, a Croatian community was established under the name of Soli, S-o-l-i; and that it also adopted the decision to join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. At this point in time, I can't remember the dates, and I'd rather not speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one minor clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You said on page 12, line 5, that it was December 1992 that Bosanska Posavina was established. Could it be December 1991 and not 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I said it was on the 12th of November, 1991. I don't know how it was recorded. If I said anything else, then I misspoke. A week before the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna this happened, or on the 12th of November, 1991, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to the next document, 1D 02258, this is again dated 12 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decision to establish the Croatian Defence Council of Banovici, and we see from the very -- from very first article, Article 1, we see that the Banovici HVO shall be engaged in defence as part of the armed forces of BH. Where is Banovici, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Banovici is in the north-eastern part of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you repeat yourself. Could you repeat that last answer, sir. Were you aware that they were part of the defence of the -- Croatian Defence --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started speaking, but I didn't know whether my microphone was still on. I am aware that the Croatian Defence Council was established in the municipality of Banovici, and that it was part of the Croatian Defence Council of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I believe that it was active in one part of the municipality of Banovici, rather than its entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then we go on to the next document, 1D 02259.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, here, we see a decision to form the military unit of the Tuzla HVO. Were you aware that there was such a unit in Tuzla? This is dated 25 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this decision which says that the HVO was established and was active in one part of the municipality of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say "part," just to make sure, to tie it in with your answer yesterday, because yesterday you corrected one of the translations when you said "areas." So when you say "part," is that what you're referring to, that these HVO units or HVO establishments were in some areas of the municipality, not the entire municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is connected with the topic I discussed yesterday. The fact of the matter is that the HVO, specifically in this case in Tuzla, was not able to be active throughout the territory of the Tuzla municipality; rather, it was active only in certain areas of that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We go to the next document, 1D 02253.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here, we see this is dated 8 July 1992. It's a decision to form administrative offices in the territory of the Croatian part of Teslic-Komusina municipality.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a case similar to the one we've just discussed. Mention is made of the administrative offices being set up in the -- in a part of the territory of these municipalities. Therefore, as the very title says, the establishment of these offices does not refer to the entire territories of these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We go on to the next document, 1D 02053, 1D 02053. We see it's dated 11 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see that this is an order, and two things that we can point out for the Judges. One is under number 1. It talks about men liable for military service, and we see the age of 18 to 60. And, of course, number 3 which may be more important and you could comment on that, where it says: "Men liable for military service from other municipalities, who are currently in the territory of Ljubuski municipality, shall be escorted to their municipalities." Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that this is an order, and an order which relates to Ljubuski municipality. This order speaks of all the issues that the municipalities had to decide upon at the time in no uncertain terms. What is typical for this particular order is that the municipalities were separate entities developing their own respective regulations. This particular order testifies to the fact that it was very difficult to organize any sort of defence in these municipalities without the HVO. What it says in this part is that the military-aged men from Ljubuski were unable to leave their territory -- the territory of their municipality and that the authorities of the Ljubuski municipality did not allow other military-aged men to enter their territory. What clearly arises from this document is that neither were the military-aged men from the Ljubuski municipality allowed to leave their municipality to help out those in other municipalities, and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... to me particularly important. You've just pointed out that the municipalities were autonomous. We see in this text that there is interference by this municipality in its use of military service because they prohibit all those aged between 18 and 60 from leaving their municipality. Should there not have been coordination at the level of the military HVO, because there is a common enemy on the face of it; and if each municipality does in its own corner wages its own individual war, there could very well be chaos or major problems. Now, this military aspect, in your view, was it relayed at the level of the HVO echelons to ensure coordination; or given the situation, did each do what they could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this particular document testifies to the state of affairs as it existed before the setting up of the 21 HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Not only is this a document which contains regulations, but it is also the reflection of the state of affairs as it existed before the joint or Main Staff was set up, which could exercise command over the armed units after the creation of the Croatian Defence Council for the entire Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It points to the difficulties that existed in these areas and to the fact that the municipalities had to defend their own territories. They had their own armies. This document also shows that military-aged men were not allowed to leave Ljubuski municipality and were unable to help out other municipalities such as Citluk, Siroki Brijeg, and others. Nor were soldiers from other municipalities able to enter Ljubuski municipality, not even to help them out, according to this particular document. This is not a document typical for Ljubuski municipality. Other municipalities issued similar regulations, but up till then municipalities acted within their competencies, which pointed to the need for the setting up of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, in order to have a unified defence, and to establish a joint command or the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, do you know whether similar problems prevailed in the Bosniak parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina? The Muslim municipalities in the same situation, did things work there more or less in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I did not receive any interpretation. I'm not receiving it still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Make a sign, if you will, if you now get a translation of my question. Still nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot speak B/C/S, but our technicians and interpreters will henceforth find a solution to this problem. Let's try again. Is it better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am certain that the municipalities with predominantly Muslim population had similar problems, but I'm also sure that in their case, the municipalities did not act in a unified or uniform way, as was the case on the Croat side for instance. There was joint command in Mostar because the Bosniaks were there. There was a 50/50 per cent division of power. The Bosniaks, Muslims, were a massive presence in the HVO in the course of 1992. The same situation prevailed in the municipality of Stolac and Konjic in the first half of 1992; whereas, in certain other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was a dominant presence of the Patriotic League as an armed wing of the Party for Democratic Action. For instance, in the area of Tuzla, there was a dominant presence of the Territorial Defence. In other areas of Tuzla municipality, there was HVO. Even on the Muslim, Bosniak, side, we come across similar problems and solutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can move on to the next document, and probably we don't need to spend so much time on this document given the questions that were asked of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decision on general mobilisation of personnel and materiel and technical equipment in the territory of Siroki Brijeg; and, here, as you indicated, different municipalities dealt with it differently. This is a decision dealing with Siroki Brijeg; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another such example. As we discussed earlier on, it is quite evident that this decision was published in the Official Gazette of the municipality of Siroki Brijeg; in other words, the Official Gazettes of municipalities were active even in times of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Buntic, for that bonus part of your answer discrediting Ribicic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection to the statement of counsel characterizing the evidence, which is in the end for the Trial Chamber to assess. I think speeches and arguments characterizing evidence don't advance the cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll move on to the next document, 1D 00591. 1D 00591. Mr. Usher, if you could help us here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a general mobilisation in the Mostar municipality; so, here, we see that this results -- we don't have a date, but it appears to result from a meeting on 21 -- on 11 July 1992. And, again, we see that it's published in the Official Gazette of the HVO Mostar municipality on the 24 July 1992, similar to what we saw the other municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should say that there is no material difference between the earlier decision relating to Siroki Brijeg municipality. As we can see, different municipalities developed their own regulations, which in some instances were similar, in others dissimilar; but they made do they best could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 02254, 1D 02254. This is a statutory decision, the Croatian Defence Council of Teslic-Komusina. Mr. Usher, we may need your assistance again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is dated, if we look on the second page, 28 July; and this is a statutory decision on temporary establishment of the executive authorities of administration in the Croatian part of Teslic municipality. Again, this would verify what you told us earlier, that the HVO presence were in parts as opposed to whole municipalities depending on the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This case also involves certain areas of municipalities. As I said earlier on, the HVO was set up in the municipalities where the Croats were not a majority but were a significant presence. As in many other cases, the HVO was set up in the areas where there was such a presence of the Croat population, in such areas that were only part of municipalities. In this particular instance, we have a statutory decision which in its very title says that it was -- that it refers to the Croat part of Teslic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And, of course, if we look at Article 3, it tells us exactly the locations, that it's to "... join the Croatian regional community which comprises the municipalities of Maglaj, Teslic, Zavidovici, Zepce, and with headquarters in Zepce"; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another issue we've already discussed. We said that out of these parts of municipalities, a community of municipalities was established with a view to organizing joint defence of the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions, I'll go on to the next document, and this is 1D 02280. Again, Mr. Usher, we will need your assistance. I apologise for having -- for taxing you on these matters, but this is the last one. 1D 02280.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see this is a decision for Orasje municipality and we don't have a particular date, but do you recall whether in the Orasje municipality there was an HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am certain that, throughout the war, there existed the HVO in Orasje, and that the Bosniaks and Croats in the municipality of Orasje fought side by side throughout the war under the title of the HVO of Orasje, and that there had never been any clashes breaking out between Bosniaks and Croats in Orasje, not even when the conflicts broke out in Central Bosnia and in Herzegovina. There had never been any clashes between Croats and Muslims in that particular territory. And what's more, they fought in the rankings of the HVO against their common enemy. This document shows, again, that in various municipalities and in various parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the wartime situation developed in different ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we'll see that with the next few documents before we leave this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a follow-up question, Mr. Witness. After the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna during this famous meeting in Grude, if we look at this. Looking at this document, afterwards, subsequently, municipalities joined the Croatian Community of HB, Herceg-Bosna, such as this municipality; is that indeed the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was indeed the case. In some instances, certain municipalities or parts thereof joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at a later date. There were also instances of complete communities of municipalities formed elsewhere joining the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I want to note, once more, that the Croatian community of Bosnian Posavina joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna later on. In this particular case, we had a fully-fledged community; whereas, in other instances, there were only individual municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good, Witness. With this document, we don't know whether there was a debate within the municipality Croat and Muslim, or if it is the president of the municipality, Mr. Dzojic, who as a member of the HDZ must decide this for himself. Do you know if there were internal discussions or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am familiar with the internal discussions that took place in the municipality of Orasje. That municipality was part of the Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina. I believe that this particular document speaks to the individual course of action taken by Orasje municipality. I believe that this document was issued earlier on, and that later on the entire Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina with all the municipalities contained therein joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a rather technical question. Did you -- have you already seen this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the document before me here. I am not sure whether I've seen the document before or not, but I have seen before a document whereby the entire Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina decided to join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I also said that I believe that the document I have before me was issued before the Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina decided to join the HZ HB. That's why I said that this particular document related to Orasje municipality only and was issued before the joining documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going well beyond my question. You're not sure whether you have seen it before or not, whether you've seen this document before. What is striking is that, although it is signed, it carries no date, and this in spite of two spaces specifically provided for indicating the date. Do you by any chance have an explanation for this? If not, I would not be surprised but I need to ask the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I've answered the question. I said that I've never seen the document before. I see it now for the first time. I have it before me, and that's why I said that this was my opinion, while saying that I'm looking at the document now for the first time. However, in view of the fact that I am aware of the internal discussions that took place in Orasje municipality, I said that I believed that this was a document issued by them autonomously. So I'm just presuming that's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go on to 1D 02255, 1D 02255.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decision on the Usora HZ joining the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we see that it's dated 20 August 1992. Were you aware of this event; that is, that there was a decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, we may need your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you can look at the document very quickly; and, again, I'm -- we have to move rather quickly.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the document. I've seen it before. Again, as I indicated earlier on, the joining party here is not a municipality but a community. The Croatian Community of Usora decides to join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I'm familiar with the document because I saw it before on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at 1D 02262, 1D 02262.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decision for Zepce municipality to join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and it's dated 21 August 1992. Just very quickly, did Zepce join the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as is reflected in this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I said in relation to the earlier document on Usora applies to this one. I'm familiar with it, I've seen it before; and, similarly, this is a municipality located in the north-eastern part of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 02257, dated 21 September 1992, 1D 02257.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, here, we see it is signed by the HVO president of Zivinice municipality, where he states: "Based on the agreement with Mr. Boban reached in Grude on setting up an HVO brigade in the four municipalities of Tuzla, Zivinice, Lukavac, and Lopari ..." and so on. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing this document before, but I know that discussions took place on this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, 1D 00265.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is a decision to establish the political and legal status of Orasje municipality, dated 29 September 1992. And, again, this would tie in to what you said earlier, but now we're talking about the Orasje municipality as a political, legal, and territorially associated unit.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the document. As is quite evident, it was published in the Official Gazette of the municipality of Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, 1D 02260, 1D 02260, dated 14 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is dealing with North-East Bosnia, Tuzla. These are conclusions from a session of the HVO of the North-East Bosnia held on 13 October 1992; and it talks about, if we look at under number 1, that the name HVO of North-East Bosnia is going to be changed, I guess, to HVO Community of Soli based in Tuzla. And I guess that's what you were referring to earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. When talking about one of the previous documents, I said that the Croatian Community of Soli was established later on, and this document speaks about that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here, we have minutes of a meeting of the HVO Banovici, Lukavac, Tuzla, and Zivinice, held on 15 December 1992. If you could look at that very quickly. And we can see, in the third paragraph, it talks about: "The Draft Statutory decision on temporary organization of executive authority and administration in the territory of the Soli HZ was read out." Again, this would tie in with your earlier remarks; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It ties in with my earlier remarks, but I've never seen this document before. It does tie in with what we have discussed so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then I think the last document in this chapter is 1D 02013.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, here, we have the statutory decision on the temporary organization of the executive government and administration in the area of the Croatian Community of Soli. So, apparently, this would tie in with the previous document that we just covered, the minutes of the meeting; and we can see from the very first article, this concerns the establishment of a body of executive -- go ahead --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The executive government and administration. And then in Article 2, which you might wish to comment, it says: "The HVO is a provisional body which shall discharge its powers until regular executive government and administration is established." Can you just briefly comment on that part before we leave this chapter?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As may be seen, this is a statutory decision on the temporary organization of executive government; and, again, I emphasize in one part of Teslic municipality, the document confirms the previous remarks about this municipality, which is also in the north-eastern part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And this decision illustrates the fact that municipalities continued to adopt decisions in order to regulate certain issues. As we have seen, some municipalities and some communities of municipalities then subsequently joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll go on to the next segment, and I want to deal with now 14 August 1992 because on that particular day there was a session of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna that was held in Grude. And we can see that from document 1D 01659, 01659.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just look at it, just go through it very quickly. If you look at it, you'll come across your name. So I suspect that you were present during that particular meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, yes. I was present at the meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- the Judges may have some questions on this document. I just wanted to point out a couple of things. One, if we go on to page 8 in the English version, I don't -- it would be under number -- it was after the report that was given by Bozo Rajic. And it would be under paragraph 6, which after the report paragraph 6, it's on page 8 in the English version. We see that there's a gentleman by the name of Ivan Azinovic, Konjic HVO. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it actually. Can you refer me to the correct page in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll try to do that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it just says here that: "Sefer Halilovic has ordered all equipment be seized from HVO, and that the HVO in this territory be declared the aggressor and a paramilitary unit. "He proposed that the convoy with humanitarian aid be allowed to pass, but only the part that contains food and after reloading, while equipment should be blocked until an agreement is reached." Were you aware of Mr. Halilovic's activities as reflected here by Mr. Azinovic in Konjic; that is, that he was seizing the equipment and declaring HVO to be the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Problems in the municipality of Konjic, as may be seen in this document, involved the HVO and BiH army or the Patriotic League. They started after the summer of 1992. As may be seen from the document, Mr. Azinovic informed the Presidency of those problems; although, before the summer of 1992, Konjic was a peaceful area in which there were no conflicts whatsoever between the HVO and the units of the Muslim or the Bosniak side. I'm also aware of the fact that a large number of skirmishes arose from the fact that Mr. Halilovic's role increased. Even Azinovic from Konjic speaks about that in this particular case. Konjic is a municipality which is north of Mostar on the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina. In other words, this is the -- in the area surrounding the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm not going to cover every instance where you spoke. The Judges may wish to question you on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's an invitation, by the way, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm going to focus your attention on page 11 under paragraph number 13, because there you do speak about the decree on the application of the Law on Court Fees. And, here, it says you gave some explanations. This would be page 12 for you in the Croatian version. So if you could just please tell us if you recall what your remarks were concerning the amendments that were made related to court fees.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under item 12, you can see that this is about the decree on the application of the RBH KZ and the SFRJ KZ in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as well as the decree on the application of the Law on Court Fees. Both decrees relative to both the republican and federal regulations, the only thing that they changed was the fact that the fees expressed in the dinars of the former Yugoslavia as the legal tender were then converted into the Croatian dinars. No other provision of any of the two laws was changed or modified by these two decrees. They were adopted verbatim as they existed before then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we heard testimony a couple of weeks ago of a gentleman who was able to assist us a little bit on financial or monetary issues in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. But very briefly, if you could tell us, why the Croatian dinar, why not the Bosnian-Herzegovinian dinar or the Deutschemark or some other currency? Why that currency?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to Yugoslav dinars at the time that we're talking about, which is August 1992, they did not exist in any of the monetary transactions in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm not a financial expert, but I believe that this may be explained by the fact that the payment transaction service that was in charge of the payments both in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the former Yugoslavia no longer functioned. Yugoslav dinars could not reach the area; and, indeed, they didn't reach the area. And at that particular time, I don't think that Bosnian dinar had been issued as a legal tender; and if it had been, then just like the Yugoslav dinar, it was exposed to the galloping inflation and devaluation. At that time, in this area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, most of the payments were effected in Croatian dinars because Croatian dinars were most easy to be had and somewhat less was carried out in German marks. We were faced with one of the possibilities then, to adopt Croatian dinar as the legal tender, and there were plenty of Croatian dinars in circulation. And the second possibility was to adopt German mark, the currency that was in very short supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And a third option, and please let me finish, was to issue one's own currency as the legal tender; and there was even a fourth option and that was to effect payments in kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I fully believe that the last option is -- was really out of the question, that it wasn't acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We're going to have to move a little bit quicker on the next few documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just a question of understanding. In the previous paragraph, number 12, one speaks of the RBH KZ. Could you tell me what "KZ" is as an abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "KZ" is the criminal law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll go on to 1D 0005, and we see that this is dated September 1992; well, the Official Gazette, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, at the bottom, we see Boban's name, 14 August 1992, and this is a decree on application of the Law on Court Duties. And then just very quickly, as you indicated, if we look at number -- if we look at Article 2, we see that the: "Dinar values stipulated in the Law on Court Duties on Municipal Tax Fees issued before this decree came into effect shall be changed into Croatian dinars ..." So that was based on the explanation you gave us earlier, correct? These are just examples for the Court to see.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This corresponds to what I previously said, but I would still like to read Article 1 which confirms what I said also. This reads: "The Law on Court Duties of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall also be applied in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." And as has already been said, everything remained the same save for the fact that Yugoslav dinars were transformed into Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And then if we look at the preamble, it also -- it also makes reference to a decision proclaiming an imminent threat of war; and it states it's the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on to the next document, P 00449, the preamble looks more or less the same as the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a decree on the application of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Again, as you indicated in your previous answer, if we look at Article 1 and then Article 2, again, it reflects the dinar value. Other than what you've already told us with respect to the previous document, which was number 5, 1D 0005, anything else to comment about this document which deals with the criminal code?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is yet another example showing that the laws of the former Yugoslavia were adopted and applied to the full, as well as the laws of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, save for those parts that mandated interventions, because without those interventions or corrections, it would not have been possible to apply these regulations. And this also refers to the criminal code.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can go on to the next document, P 00440, P 00440.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is a decree on the organization and responsibilities of the departments and commissions of the Croatian Defence Council. And perhaps if you could tell us a little bit about what exactly these commissions are about, just very briefly, one sentence, and then I'll focus you to a particular article.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree regulates commissions as special, professional, technical bodies established by the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I know that there were, for example, commissions: A commission for regulations, a commission for restructuring and development, and that there was also, for example, a commission for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at Article 7, we see that: "Departments and commissions of the HVO shall cooperate with the republican bodies in the preparation of acts which confirm the policy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the preparation of laws and other regulations and general acts, referring to issues of the equality of the constituent peoples of the Republic after Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, if you could comment on that a little bit because it may be of some interest to the Judges, keeping in mind this is 14 August 1992. Here, HVO clearly, Article 7, says that they shall cooperate, and it would appear that the cooperation is to be with the state.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As may be seen from the text of this regulation, of its Article 7, that is, it points to cooperation between the departments and commissions with the republican bodies. And as it may be seen here, they're supposed to cooperate in the preparation of the documents of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina concerning the issue of equality of constituent peoples. In addition to what is contained in the Article 7 of this regulation, I believe that this regulation was motivated by the previously signed agreement between the president of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, and Franjo Tudjman in Medjugorje. That agreement called for cooperation between the HVO of the HZ HB and the republican bodies. That is why according to that agreement it was necessary to establish certain commissions and bodies which would be tasked with finding a peaceful solution within the framework offered by the European Community during the peace talks about Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that helps us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, P -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I follow your advice, and I ask a question. The Article 7 which you referred to and Mr. Buntic answered this question, your question. I would only like to ask you, Mr. Buntic, about the following: Article 7 speaks about the cooperation, but somehow it is not very clear for me when it says that departments and commissions of the HVO shall cooperate with the republican bodies in preparation of acts, et cetera. And, again, in the second paragraph, it also says the: "Departments and commissions of the HVO shall cooperate with administrative bodies of other states ..." Now, as far as the first part of Article 7 is concerned, it speaks about cooperation, as I already mentioned this, but I do not see how the cooperation is being followed in case e filaci [phoen]. There are certain divergent views or whatever the means to reach some conclusions, to reach some compromises, et cetera, because here we speak only about cooperation but there is no mention of the hierarchical, in a way, acting in conformity of the laws and regulations adopted by the republic; that is, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And in other words, the cooperation before me in this sense would only mean that there is cooperation between and among equals. This article suggests that the major position of that time of HVO was that it was a cooperation among equals, because we do not find here anything which would indicate that in terms of discussion or disagreements what kind of laws and regulations should be applied. It is my question that, in case of conflicts between two regimes, let's say regime as applied and as established in Herceg-Bosna and regime as applied and, of course, established by the republican bodies in Sarajevo, what was the mechanism which would overcome the divergencies of views and rules?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the previous decrees passed by the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which is the decree on the application of the criminal code, the decree on the application of the Law on Criminal Procedure, on judicial fees, as well as of all the other regulations passed by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, it is obvious that all these decrees -- laws were adopted in full, save for in those parts where interventions were necessary. And when I spoke about the interventions, I said what those interventions were; like, for example, when Yugoslav dinars were transformed into Croatian dinars in order for the law to be applied. When we're talking about this, I believe that what is striking is the cooperation with other states. But in my previous answer, I said that this Article 7 was by and large motivated by the previously signed agreement between Messrs. Tudjman and Izetbegovic, as presidents of two states. This agreement envisaged the establishment of certain commissions which would work to overcome and find solutions to the problems that existed at the time and coordinating all the regulations. As a result of all that, immediately after the meeting between Tudjman and Izetbegovic in Medjugorje, I had a meeting with the deputy minister of justice of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we discussed the issues of judiciary. It was this conversation between the minister of justice of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and me that took place in Medjugorje which resulted in the decree on the fact that the decree on military courts was never published and it was never applied. In keeping with our agreement, me and Mr. Jusuf Halilagic, the deputy minister of justice of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at our session on the 17th of October, we adopted a new decree on district military courts and district military prosecutor's offices, which was published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and which was applied in practice, and which was coordinated with the positions of the republican Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Buntic, for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you indicated that the decrees on the military courts were not implemented, you were referring to P 09552 of 3 July 1992 that we spoke of yesterday, and I cut you off and I said we will cover that later on; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's the decree I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission, yesterday, in answer to Their Honours' question about subdepartments, this is something that we discussed. And this particular decree in Article 12 regulates the setting up of departments and subdepartments, both Articles 12 and 19. Article 19 lists all the subdepartments within the HVO. As we can see, there is a total of 13 of them. That's why I had difficulties yesterday in listing them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I have one follow-up question, but we can take care of that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We are going to break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, I want to go back to the question that was asked of you by Judge Prandler. This is a follow-up question; and when I look at the question, it would appear that at least the impression is that from reading this particular article, that the Judge believes that you have two different states operating in the same territory, two different regimes; in other words, that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is a state within a state. Could you please explain to us, was that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the case, nor do I believe that this is what follows from Article 7 and the meaning it conveys. I have already talked about what I believe the -- what it was that immediately motivated Article 7. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna recognised and never called into question the sovereignty and independence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This follows from all of its documents, wherein almost every heading of the document, you can read Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and then below that Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. In addition to that, all of the regulations passed by the HZ HB state clearly that those were merely provisional regulations valid only while there was a state of war. These regulations were the result of necessity, and we were able to see that the regulations were passed only for those areas where it was strictly necessary in order for the legislation of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be applied. We were able to see for ourselves, based on the enactments, decrees, and regulations we looked at before, that these were passed only where it was strictly necessary. I don't believe that this particular article implies that there were two states in existence. Simply, these were entities that were treated as such, that through peacemaking negotiations aimed at finding a settlement of the crisis, all the three parties to these negotiations were treated as equals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas, but I would like to thank Mr. Buntic for his answer, and I have to be very frank that I'm grateful to you, too, because you asked your question which was my question, too. But I was probably more cautious than you were and that is why you put it in shorter form. But I admit that it was my original intention to ask this question because the same Article 7 speaks about a cooperation with the authorities of the republic. And, also, at the same time, in the second paragraph, it speaks about the cooperation with other states. So that is why I asked the question. And I thank you both for the answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on to the next document, P 00429.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see that it's dated 14 August 1992, and we see that this is a decision on the election of the president of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Dr. Jadranko Prlic. You would confirm that it was on this day that this decision was passed; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I talked about this decision yesterday. It was passed on the 14th of August, 1992. I said that Mr. Jadranko Prlic was appointed president of the HVO only on the 14th of August, 1992. So, yes, that's the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please explain to us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, you were in Grude because your name is indicated. I'm trying to understand this election. Is it the fact that Mr. Boban had far too much work because he had several hats, or is it because those who voted for Mr. Prlic were trying to better control Mr. Boban by putting in place someone from the election of the municipalities? In this election, did it have political significance or was it a reorganization of the powers or no purpose whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there were various reasons, as we were able to see yesterday. In the period running up to the 14th of August, that's to say mid-August 1992, all the powers were in the hands of Mr. Mate Boban, who, as we were able to see yesterday, was the president of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the president of the HVO, therefore, of the executive government as well, and the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which was a third function. He was also the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces; that is to say, of the military section of the HVO. And he was also deputy president of the Croatian Democratic Union, the strongest Croat political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina which had as its followers 95 per cent of the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It could be said that all the powers were concentrated in the hands of Mr. Mate Boban alone. One of the reasons might well have been the fact that he could no longer carry all the various hats that he had. Another reason could have been an attempt at separating the various powers, the legislative from the executive power. The attempt was made through the decree of the 3rd of July, which was, in fact, implemented only on the 14th of August, in such a way that the executive civilian authority got as its president Mr. Jadranko Prlic. This relates to the civilian segment or the executive branch of authority of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, whereby the then-hitherto president, Mate Boban, was replaced by Jadranko Prlic. After that, Mr. Mate Boban held to all the other different functions that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Buntic, prior to August 14, 1992, how much work was actually done by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were able to see that, up until the 14th of August, heads of offices or departments of the Croatian Defence Council had been appointed: The head of the defence department, head of the department of the interior, head of the department of justice and general administration, and head of the department for the economy, I believe. I'm not sure whether Mr. Prlic, prior to this appointment, had been appointed head of the finance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But other than these appointments, concretely, how much legislation had been passed? How many meetings were held? How much actual work was done?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the first meeting of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was at the same time a constituent meeting of the HZ HB on the 18th of November, 1991. The second meeting, as arises from some of the documents, was held on the 15th of May of 1992. A third meeting was held on the 3rd of July, 1992. The 14th of August meeting was the fourth meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB. It's difficult for me to cite the exact number of decrees or decisions taken by the Presidency of the HZ HB; however, on the basis of the various minutes and documents we were able to see here, we can conclude that a number of regulations in the form of decrees was passed, as well as decisions that certain appointments to certain posts within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me be a little more specific. How many meetings between the heads of departments were held prior to the 14th of August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the HVO is concerned, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. This was my --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to that executive branch of government, not a single meeting had been held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on now, we're going to go on to a transcript of a meeting 17 September 1992. It's 1D 02366.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't have time to cover it all. The Judges may have questions. This meeting took place in Zagreb, and I just want to look at two portions of it and then have you comment; and then if the Judges wish to ask you to -- to ask any further questions, that would be fine. In this particular instance, you do recall being at this meeting on 17 September 1992, do you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were you aware at the time, by the way, that you were being tape recorded, you, along with everybody else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that we were being taped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at page 27 in the English version where Mr. Prlic begins speaking towards the bottom, that's where it starts. And I'm going to go to actually page 28, and there he talks about what the Serbs want or their option, the Muslim option; and then he comes to the Croat option, and that would be on the fourth paragraph on page 28 in English. He says, and I quote: "The Croats, at least the soldiers in the Croatian Defence Council and the people who are involved, the organs of authority, have a clear political aim. It has been clear to me ever since I became involved in this and since I have been in this post. This aim is the forming and ordering of Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the principles of the European Community; that is, the constituting of Bosnia and Herzegovina through three national units." Now, let's just move on, just think about that, and I want to go to where you speak. This would be on page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You will note, Your Honours, that this has a different number, this document, because we translated pages that were not translated by the Prosecution, this being an excerpt of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here, we have you speaking and you talk about the situation, and I'll just read portions of it. You say: "I think we must make a distinction between important and unimportant facts, i.e., between contested and uncontested ones. I would count the following as important and uncontested fact. Firstly, according to the current Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it is defined as a complex state consisting of three constitutive elements. Secondly, I do not know of any other multi-ethnic community in the world arranged in accordance with the unitary principle. Thirdly, since the beginning of the peace talks on Bosnia-Herzegovina under the agencies of the international community, the findings of the Badinter Commission, the European Community, and the United Nations have been offering a solution to the effect; that is to say, configuring Bosnia-Herzegovina as a complex state ." I won't read the rest, the Judges may have some questions, and it is rather interesting. Due to time, I simply cannot. Having heard of what Dr. Prlic said and now having heard your own words or parts of them, could you please explain to us what is being said here.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall being at this meeting held on the 17th of September, 1992. Its purpose -- or rather, it followed an earlier meeting in preparation for the London Conference, peace conference, to find a resolution to the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was organized by the international community. That was the reason why this meeting was held in Zagreb. At this meeting, those of us from Bosnia-Herzegovina presented our views which we believed we were supposed to advocate at the peace conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina. I remember the fact that the speech by Jadranko Prlic is mostly reflected in this transcript, and that it, indeed, tallies with what you've read out. I can also confirm that my intervention, the part which you cited, is accurate or is accurately reflected in the part that you've read out. It is also true that I spoke more extensively than is reflected here, but that the part you quoted does constitute the gist of what our discussion was about and of what Mr. Prlic and I advocated at that meeting. The position we advanced was that of the HVO, of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and it was the subject of discussion at a meeting which preceded the visit to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions from the Bench, I will go on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, without doubt, the intervention of Mr. Prlic during this meeting and yours are crucial interventions and really at the heart of the indictment; and so I must, therefore, ask you a follow-up question. When we compare what Mr. Prlic says and what you yourself state, it is almost the same thing with just a few nuances. But your intervention before President Tudjman, you're at some point interrupted by someone who says: "That's not true." President Tudjman says to the speaker: "Wait a moment. Let Mr. Buntic finish and you will speak after him." And you ended on the question of the platform, and the person who doesn't agree with you is Mr. Vlado Pandzic. I don't know who that person is but you will tell us, and this Pandzic rejects your comments and notably through question of the HDZ platform. And it would appear that he states the following: That the Croatian people is sovereign in Bosnia-Herzegovina and would seem to challenge the legality of the other ethnic groups. In other words, he takes the opposite view. Then there are other speakers who take the floor, and I'd like to know ultimately what is Mr. Tudjman's conclusion; but, unfortunately, not all the pages have been translated. I find no trace of the conclusion. Do you recall, because to be in the presence of a head of state, that isn't an everyday occurrence. So you no doubt have in your mind a specific recollection of that meeting and the fact that Vlado Pandzic interrupted you. Who is this Mr. Vlado Pandzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlado Pandzic is a member of the Croatian Democratic Union. I think he was on the executive committee or the Presidency of the HVO, and I believe he was deputy in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The discussion between Mr. Pandzic and myself had to do with the fact that - if I remember correctly - I was critical of Mr. Pandzic. I criticised the HDZ for not having come forth with their own proposals as to what the future structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina should be, for not having come up with that proposal within the framework of the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We're referring to it here as a platform, although -- or rather, both the SDS and the SDA had come up with their own proposals, and I criticised the HDZ for not having taken up their own position as to the future structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina while the BH parliament was still in session. Mr. Pandzic's view was different from mine. He believed that they had a firm position on that. The discussion between Mr. Pandzic and myself revolved around that issue.
